1	# Package identity
2	
3	How the workspace names packages, why bare names match across ecosystems, and where platform packages are wired in. Behavior: [`docs/specs/workspace.json`](../specs/workspace.json). Config keys: [`docs/config.md`](../config.md). Platform ownership decision: [ADR 7](../adr/0007-platform-packages-owned-through-optional-dependencies.md).
4	
5	## Terms
6	
7	- Dual-manifest package: one directory with several admitted canonical manifests; one graph package, one version grammar and several distribution identities. Cargo+npm is supported by the model; co-located Cargo+Python currently fails with E007 because their grammars differ, including a Maturin dynamic Python version.
8	- Co-located platform manifest: an `os`+`cpu` `package.json` in the same directory as its owner's `Cargo.toml`.
9	- Attached platform package: an `os`+`cpu` `package.json` in its own directory, owned via another package's `optionalDependencies`.
10	
11	## `PackageId` (`crates/callisto-model/src/identity.rs`)
12	
13	| Form | Example | `ecosystem()` |
14	| --- | --- | --- |
15	| `Bare(name)` | `foo`, `@scope/foo` | `None` |
16	| `Prefixed { ecosystem, name }` | `cargo/foo`, `npm/@scope/foo` | `Some(e)` |
17	
18	- `parse` treats text before the first `/` as a prefix only when `Ecosystem::from_prefix` knows it, so `@scope/foo` stays bare. It still reads `cargo:foo`; every user-facing input rejects that form with E316 first.
19	- `display_name` renders a prefixed id as `ecosystem/name`.
20	- `PackageId` is the display and selector form; `Package::key()` is the workspace-relative directory of the first canonical manifest. It survives display promotion, not a directory move. `ReleasePackageId` names each canonical distribution as `ecosystem/name` using that manifest's own native name.
21	- Default tags use `display_name()`: `foo@{version}` while bare, `cargo/foo@{version}` after promotion. Promotion therefore also changes the namespace of newly created default tags (ADR 11).
22	- `matches` is a weak "could be the same package" relation, not equality:
23	  - Different names never match.
24	  - A bare id matches any id with the same name, in either direction: bare is an ecosystem wildcard.
25	  - Two prefixed ids match only when their ecosystems are equal.
26	- A dual-manifest package can have different native names. `IdentityIndex` resolves each ecosystem/name to its owner; the weak `matches` relation alone does not establish distribution identity or ownership.
27	
28	## Resolving ambiguity
29	
30	A workspace can hold `cargo/foo` and `npm/foo` as separate packages; ambiguity is resolved where a lookup happens. Qualified selectors work before and after promotion, and the colon form is rejected with E316. Canonical-only new references are planned in [the v1 design](polyglot-v1.md), not implemented by today's parser.
31	
32	- `aggregate::resolve_target_package` resolves changeset entries through `IdentityIndex::resolve_id`, which maps qualified native distribution names to their owner and rejects ambiguous bare names. `status` attributes changeset entries and checks their well-formedness through the same resolver. `PackageId::resolve_unique` scans display ids, is deprecated, and is not equivalent for dual-manifest packages with different native names.
33	- `[[package]]` rules use `config::resolve::resolve_package_config`: the first rule in declaration order whose ecosystem the package has and whose name matches. It never sorts the rules. Config rejects a rule without its ecosystem (E317), so every rule is ecosystem-qualified.
34	- `[[package-set]]` is a fallback applied in `ManifestWalkResolver::build` (`crates/callisto-graph/src/walk.rs`) only when no `[[package]]` rule matched. Patterns (`config/pattern.rs`) are globs over the name with an optional ecosystem prefix, tested against every ecosystem the package has a manifest in.
35	
36	## Loading a workspace
37	
38	`Workspace::load` (`crates/callisto-graph/src/lib.rs`):
39	
40	1. `config::load` reads `callisto.toml` (absent means empty) and calls `config::resolve`, which does all validation and defaulting. Callers holding a `RawConfig` in memory call `resolve` directly.
41	2. `ManifestWalkResolver::build` discovers projects, assigns ids (`IdentityIndex`), attaches platform packages and applies per-package config.
42	3. `GroupTable::resolve` binds group members to ids.
43	4. The tag index is built lazily, on the first `Workspace::tags` call.
44	
45	A Cargo package inherits from the Cargo workspace that governs it, found the way Cargo finds it (`cargo::enclosing_workspace_manifest`): `package.workspace`, else the nearest manifest at or above the package with a `workspace` table, never above the workspace root. That workspace can be below the root, so the walk, the version guard, release-commit verification, lockfile refresh and `registry_argv` all resolve it per package. Cargo does not judge membership for inheritance, and neither does this lookup: a root that excludes or omits the package is a repository Cargo itself rejects.
46	
47	`Workspace::load` returns only a complete workspace, and it is the only way to get one. Every manifest the walk cannot open (for its platform role, publish targets or dependencies) is recorded as an error-level `ManifestUnresolved` diagnostic, and `load` turns any of them into E313 naming each manifest once, so no command sees a roster smaller than the repository.
48	
49	## Historical ownership
50	
51	For a promoted package, `TagIndex::build` also considers bare-name tags. `history::sole_owner_at` picks the same-named candidate whose first canonical manifest path held a manifest declaring the name at the tag's commit. When none does, because the directory moved or the package gained a higher-priority manifest, it asks which ecosystems had a manifest declaring the shared name at that commit, found with `git grep` and confirmed by reading only the matching manifests. The owner is the one candidate whose own manifest in such an ecosystem has that native name today, taken from the identity index. Two or more matches, or none, mean no owner. `assign_promoted_pre_keys` applies the same check at the commit that added `pre.json`, and E245 reports a baseline with no unique owner. A bare key that matches one current package is checked too: if `pre.json` was added when a manifest of another ecosystem held the name and the package had none, the key pins nothing.
52	
53	A package that is not promoted checks its own tags the same way: `TagIndex::build` takes the newest `{name}@` tag only if `history::may_have_held_name_at` finds that the tag's commit did not hold a manifest of another ecosystem under the name. A commit with no manifest under the name, or one that cannot be read, is no evidence, so the tag is taken. A rejected tag is reported as `tag-owned-by-another-package` and is not counted as a release of the package.
54	
55	A demoted package, whose same-named sibling was removed, also considers the qualified tags of its first manifest's ecosystem and keeps the newest version across both families.
56	
57	A rename that changes the native name, or a move that changes it too, leaves no evidence in Git. Declare it with `previous-tag-templates`; do not infer it from the directory key.
58	
59	## Platform packages in code
60	
61	| Step | Where |
62	| --- | --- |
63	| Find candidates outside the npm workspace globs | `ProjectLocator::projects_and_platform_candidates` |
64	| Attach a platform to its single owner, or warn | `platform_owners` in `walk.rs` |
65	| Look up a platform's owner by the platform's own npm name | `IdentityIndex::platform` |
66	| List an owner's attached platforms (co-located ones excluded) | `IdentityIndex::attached_platforms` |
67	| Write the owner's version into platform manifests and pin `optionalDependencies` | `platform_version_writes` in `commands/version.rs` (version and snapshot) |
68	| Publish each platform before its owner | `commands/release/derive.rs`: one `PlatformPublish` operation per attached platform |
69	
70	- A `PlatformPublish` operation carries the owner's package id and version, so it passes the intent's check that every operation belongs to a decision entry, and each one is a prerequisite of the owner's npm `RegistryPublish`.
71	- It gets no tag, forge or artifact operation of its own; it publishes by directory.
72	- Release identities come from `release_package_ids` (`commands/release_decision.rs`): one per canonical manifest, using that manifest's own name, so a dual-manifest package with different Cargo and npm names releases under both.

# Package identity

How the workspace names packages, why bare names match across ecosystems, and where platform packages are wired in. Behavior: [`docs/specs/workspace.json`](../specs/workspace.json). Config keys: [`docs/config.md`](../config.md). Platform ownership decision: [ADR 7](../adr/0007-platform-packages-owned-through-optional-dependencies.md).

## Terms

- Dual-manifest package: one directory with several admitted canonical manifests; one graph package, one version grammar and several distribution identities. Cargo+npm is supported by the model; co-located Cargo+Python currently fails with E007 because their grammars differ, including a Maturin dynamic Python version.
- Co-located platform manifest: an `os`+`cpu` `package.json` in the same directory as its owner's `Cargo.toml`.
- Attached platform package: an `os`+`cpu` `package.json` in its own directory, owned via another package's `optionalDependencies`.

## `PackageId` (`crates/callisto-model/src/identity.rs`)

| Form | Example | `ecosystem()` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Bare(name)` | `foo`, `@scope/foo` | `None` |
| `Prefixed { ecosystem, name }` | `cargo/foo`, `npm/@scope/foo` | `Some(e)` |

- `parse` treats text before the first `/` as a prefix only when `Ecosystem::from_prefix` knows it, so `@scope/foo` stays bare. It still reads `cargo:foo`; every user-facing input rejects that form with E316 first.
- `display_name` renders a prefixed id as `ecosystem/name`.
- `PackageId` is the display and selector form; `Package::key()` is the workspace-relative directory of the first canonical manifest. It survives display promotion, not a directory move. `ReleasePackageId` names each canonical distribution as `ecosystem/name` using that manifest's own native name.
- Default tags use `display_name()`: `foo@{version}` while bare, `cargo/foo@{version}` after promotion. Promotion therefore also changes the namespace of newly created default tags (ADR 11).
- `matches` is a weak "could be the same package" relation, not equality:
  - Different names never match.
  - A bare id matches any id with the same name, in either direction: bare is an ecosystem wildcard.
  - Two prefixed ids match only when their ecosystems are equal.
- A dual-manifest package can have different native names. `IdentityIndex` resolves each ecosystem/name to its owner; the weak `matches` relation alone does not establish distribution identity or ownership.

## Resolving ambiguity

A workspace can hold `cargo/foo` and `npm/foo` as separate packages; ambiguity is resolved where a lookup happens. Qualified selectors work before and after promotion, and the colon form is rejected with E316. Canonical-only new references are planned in [the v1 design](polyglot-v1.md), not implemented by today's parser.

- `aggregate::resolve_target_package` resolves changeset entries through `IdentityIndex::resolve_id`, which maps qualified native distribution names to their owner and rejects ambiguous bare names. `status` attributes changeset entries and checks their well-formedness through the same resolver. `PackageId::resolve_unique` scans display ids, is deprecated, and is not equivalent for dual-manifest packages with different native names.
- `[[package]]` rules use `config::resolve::resolve_package_config`: the first rule in declaration order whose ecosystem the package has and whose name matches. It never sorts the rules. Config rejects a rule without its ecosystem (E317), so every rule is ecosystem-qualified.
- `[[package-set]]` is a fallback applied in `ManifestWalkResolver::build` (`crates/callisto-graph/src/walk.rs`) only when no `[[package]]` rule matched. Patterns (`config/pattern.rs`) are globs over the name with an optional ecosystem prefix, tested against every ecosystem the package has a manifest in.

## Loading a workspace

`Workspace::load` (`crates/callisto-graph/src/lib.rs`):

1. `config::load` reads `callisto.toml` (absent means empty) and calls `config::resolve`, which does all validation and defaulting. Callers holding a `RawConfig` in memory call `resolve` directly.
2. `ManifestWalkResolver::build` discovers projects, assigns ids (`IdentityIndex`), attaches platform packages and applies per-package config.
3. `GroupTable::resolve` binds group members to ids.
4. The tag index is built lazily, on the first `Workspace::tags` call.

A Cargo package inherits from the Cargo workspace that governs it, found the way Cargo finds it (`cargo::enclosing_workspace_manifest`): `package.workspace`, else the nearest manifest at or above the package with a `workspace` table, never above the workspace root. That workspace can be below the root, so the walk, the version guard, release-commit verification, lockfile refresh and `registry_argv` all resolve it per package. Cargo does not judge membership for inheritance, and neither does this lookup: a root that excludes or omits the package is a repository Cargo itself rejects.

`Workspace::load` returns only a complete workspace, and it is the only way to get one. Every manifest the walk cannot open (for its platform role, publish targets or dependencies) is recorded as an error-level `ManifestUnresolved` diagnostic, and `load` turns any of them into E313 naming each manifest once, so no command sees a roster smaller than the repository.

## Historical ownership

For a promoted package, `TagIndex::build` also considers bare-name tags. `history::sole_owner_at` picks the same-named candidate whose first canonical manifest path held a manifest declaring the name at the tag's commit. When none does, because the directory moved or the package gained a higher-priority manifest, it asks which ecosystems had a manifest declaring the shared name at that commit, found with `git grep` and confirmed by reading only the matching manifests. The owner is the one candidate whose own manifest in such an ecosystem has that native name today, taken from the identity index. Two or more matches, or none, mean no owner. `assign_promoted_pre_keys` applies the same check at the commit that added `pre.json`, and E245 reports a baseline with no unique owner. A bare key that matches one current package is checked too: if `pre.json` was added when a manifest of another ecosystem held the name and the package had none, the key pins nothing.

A package that is not promoted checks its own tags the same way: `TagIndex::build` takes the newest `{name}@` tag only if `history::may_have_held_name_at` finds that the tag's commit did not hold a manifest of another ecosystem under the name. A commit with no manifest under the name, or one that cannot be read, is no evidence, so the tag is taken. A rejected tag is reported as `tag-owned-by-another-package` and is not counted as a release of the package.

A demoted package, whose same-named sibling was removed, also considers the qualified tags of its first manifest's ecosystem and keeps the newest version across both families.

A rename that changes the native name, or a move that changes it too, leaves no evidence in Git. Declare it with `previous-tag-templates`; do not infer it from the directory key.

## Platform packages in code

| Step | Where |
| --- | --- |
| Find candidates outside the npm workspace globs | `ProjectLocator::projects_and_platform_candidates` |
| Attach a platform to its single owner, or warn | `platform_owners` in `walk.rs` |
| Look up a platform's owner by the platform's own npm name | `IdentityIndex::platform` |
| List an owner's attached platforms (co-located ones excluded) | `IdentityIndex::attached_platforms` |
| Write the owner's version into platform manifests and pin `optionalDependencies` | `platform_version_writes` in `commands/version.rs` (version and snapshot) |
| Publish each platform before its owner | `commands/release/derive.rs`: one `PlatformPublish` operation per attached platform |

- A `PlatformPublish` operation carries the owner's package id and version, so it passes the intent's check that every operation belongs to a decision entry, and each one is a prerequisite of the owner's npm `RegistryPublish`.
- It gets no tag, forge or artifact operation of its own; it publishes by directory.
- Release identities come from `release_package_ids` (`commands/release_decision.rs`): one per canonical manifest, using that manifest's own name, so a dual-manifest package with different Cargo and npm names releases under both.

1	# Release execution
2	
3	The types that make a release run safe to crash and rerun, and how the two release routes share them. Behavior: [`docs/specs/release.json`](../specs/release.json). Operator guide: [`docs/releasing.md`](../releasing.md). Decisions: ADRs [2](../adr/0002-committed-decision-is-release-authority.md), [3](../adr/0003-reruns-adopt-landed-effects.md), [4](../adr/0004-ecosystem-tools-publish-and-own-auth.md) and [7](../adr/0007-platform-packages-owned-through-optional-dependencies.md).
4	
5	## Terms
6	
7	- Package: a dependency-graph node owned by a directory; it can expose several canonical manifest/distribution identities.
8	- Distribution identity: `ReleasePackageId`, an ecosystem-qualified native package name. A graph package with several identities has one tag, one forge release and one forge publish, each carried by the package's owner: its first selected identity in manifest order (Cargo, then npm, then PyPI).
9	- Artifact: the bytes of one *(package, version, target)*, declared by `[[release.artifact]]`. It has no version, tag or changelog of its own. Callisto does not parse `target`; CI supplies product-slot bytes and Callisto records where they go. Registry publishing can invoke native build/pack tools, including Python's build backend.
10	- Product package: `[release].product-package`. Every artifact slot uploads to the product's one GitHub Release, even when another package built the bytes (`ArtifactSlotId.package`).
11	- Decision: the package and version roster (`ReleaseDecisionV1`).
12	- Intent: the decision plus the source snapshot, every operation with its prerequisites, and the artifact slots, sealed by a digest (`ReleaseIntentV1`).
13	- Operation: one effect on one provider, identified by package, version and role: registry publish, platform publish, tag, forge release (draft), artifact upload, forge publish. The operations form a DAG by prerequisite; `callisto_model::canonical_operation_order`, built on `michi-graph`, validates it (a cycle is reported as one operation on it) and fixes the order: the smallest topological order by operation id.
14	
15	## Layers
16	
17	| Layer | Crate | Contents |
18	| --- | --- | --- |
19	| Authorities | `callisto-model` (MIT) | Run envelope and execution state (`release/execution.rs`), observations and evidence (`release_observation.rs`), transition table (`release_transition.rs`) |
20	| Derivation and execution | `callisto-graph` | Decisions (`commands/release_decision.rs`), intent derivation (`commands/release/derive.rs`), local route (`commands/release/local.rs`), executor (`commands/release_execution.rs`), provider adapters (`commands/release/provider/`) |
21	| Entry points | `callisto-cli` | `commands/release.rs`: `release`, `release plan`, `release build-python`, `release artifact-manifest`, `release execute` |
22	
23	## Two routes, one executor
24	
25	```
26	local:  derive_release_roster (untagged versions, plus tagged-on-HEAD releases not fully observed)  -> plan_local_release -> intent
27	CI:     committed decision file, or --package over plan_version -> release plan -> intent -> build -> release execute
28	both:   intent -> ReleaseRunEnvelopeV1::new -> execute_release -> ReleaseReceiptV1::from_state
29	```
30	
31	- `plan_local_release` is the one derivation behind both `callisto release --dry-run` and the real run.
32	- A tag proves only that the tag was created. `incomplete_tagged_releases` observes every operation of the packages tagged on HEAD and keeps any not exactly satisfied; a tag on another commit is never observed.
33	- `ci_release_route` sends a workspace with artifact slots or platform builds to the CI route before anything runs.
34	- `expand_selection` (group members) and `require_dependencies_selected` (unselected unreleased dependencies) apply to both routes.
35	
36	## Managed release PR and workflow
37	
38	Callisto's own [release workflow](../../.github/workflows/callisto-release.yml) reconstructs one `callisto/version-packages` PR from `main` when changesets land. It versions manifests and changelogs; merging the PR consumes the changesets on `main` and authorizes publication.
39	
40	- The action commits non-workflow changes through `createCommitOnBranch`, then moves the release ref through REST. It does not run a local `git push`. Workflow files remain unchanged, so the built-in `GITHUB_TOKEN` needs no workflow-write permission.
41	- Commits are GitHub-signed as `github-actions[bot]`. An App or fine-grained token can use another identity.
42	- Branch protection must require reviews and CI checks. CODEOWNERS alone does not enforce review.
43	- `version-pr` maintains the PR; `release` runs the local release route. Artifact and platform packages use plan/build/execute. Deprecated `publish` and `create_github_release` action inputs are ignored. The [action manifest](../../.github/actions/callisto-action/action.yml) defines current inputs and outputs.
44	- Only `execute` receives registry credentials. Plan and build jobs receive none. Temporary intent, receipt, artifacts, and build output live under `RUNNER_TEMP`, outside the checkout.
45	
46	GitHub Actions schedules jobs, transports artifacts, and injects credentials. Callisto validates source, provenance, plan, observations, transitions, terminality, receipts, and artifacts. Workflow shell must not reimplement those semantics. Recovery dispatch uses current orchestration on `main` with an explicit merged source SHA and runs credential-free `recovery-checks` instead of full `verify`.
47	
48	The generated release action maps credentials without changing owner-defined publish hooks:
49	
50	- npm: copy existing user config to a mode-0600 temporary file, add an npmjs entry interpolating `NPM_TOKEN`, point npm-compatible tools at it, and remove it on exit. The original config is unchanged. `NPM_TOKEN` remains available for native hooks and `.npmrc` interpolation. Custom registries use native configuration.
51	- Bun: also set `NPM_CONFIG_TOKEN`, because Bun does not honor `NPM_CONFIG_USERCONFIG`.

## Terms

- Package: a dependency-graph node owned by a directory; it can expose several canonical manifest/distribution identities.
- Distribution identity: `ReleasePackageId`, an ecosystem-qualified native package name. A graph package with several identities has one tag, one forge release and one forge publish, each carried by the package's owner: its first selected identity in manifest order (Cargo, then npm, then PyPI).
- Artifact: the bytes of one *(package, version, target)*, declared by `[[release.artifact]]`. It has no version, tag or changelog of its own. Callisto does not parse `target`; CI supplies product-slot bytes and Callisto records where they go. Registry publishing can invoke native build/pack tools, including Python's build backend.
- Product package: `[release].product-package`. Every artifact slot uploads to the product's one GitHub Release, even when another package built the bytes (`ArtifactSlotId.package`).
- Decision: the package and version roster (`ReleaseDecisionV1`).
- Intent: the decision plus the source snapshot, every operation with its prerequisites, and the artifact slots, sealed by a digest (`ReleaseIntentV1`).
- Operation: one effect on one provider, identified by package, version and role: registry publish, platform publish, tag, forge release (draft), artifact upload, forge publish. The operations form a DAG by prerequisite; `callisto_model::canonical_operation_order`, built on `michi-graph`, validates it (a cycle is reported as one operation on it) and fixes the order: the smallest topological order by operation id.

## Layers

| Layer | Crate | Contents |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Authorities | `callisto-model` (MIT) | Run envelope and execution state (`release/execution.rs`), observations and evidence (`release_observation.rs`), transition table (`release_transition.rs`) |

CI:     committed decision file, or --package over plan_version -> release plan -> intent -> build -> release execute

5	## Documents
6	
7	| Document | Where it lives | Writes | Reads | Another version |
8	| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
9	| `ReleaseDecisionV1` | `.callisto/release-decision.json`; embedded in every intent | 2 | 1 and 2 | Version 1 is accepted and rebuilt in memory as version 2. Any other version fails to decode; reading the committed file reports E166. |
10	| `ReleaseInputSnapshotV1` | inside an intent only | 1 | any version when decoded alone | Checked only by the intent decoder, which accepts 1 only. |
11	| `ReleaseIntentV1` | `release plan --out`; the input of `release execute` and `release artifact-manifest` | 5 | 5 | Rejected before any output file is written or provider is touched: E215 from the CLI pre-check, E295 from the model decoder. |
12	| `ArtifactManifestV1` | `release artifact-manifest --out` | 1 | any version | No decode-time gate. A parse failure is E237; `validate_for_intent` accepts version 1 only. |
13	| `ReleaseRunEnvelopeV1` | inside a receipt only | 3 | 3 | Rejected at decode with an `UnsupportedSchema` error that has no diagnostic code. |

# Release wire compatibility

Which version each release document writes, which versions it reads, and what a reader does with any other. Behavior: [`docs/specs/release.json`](../specs/release.json). Release types: [`release.md`](release.md). This is a record of current behavior, not a policy; gaps are listed as gaps.

## Documents

| Document | Where it lives | Writes | Reads | Another version |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `ReleaseDecisionV1` | `.callisto/release-decision.json`; embedded in every intent | 2 | 1 and 2 | Version 1 is accepted and rebuilt in memory as version 2. Any other version fails to decode; reading the committed file reports E166. |
| `ReleaseInputSnapshotV1` | inside an intent only | 1 | any version when decoded alone | Checked only by the intent decoder, which accepts 1 only. |
| `ReleaseIntentV1` | `release plan --out`; the input of `release execute` and `release artifact-manifest` | 5 | 5 | Rejected before any output file is written or provider is touched: E215 from the CLI pre-check, E295 from the model decoder. |
| `ArtifactManifestV1` | `release artifact-manifest --out` | 1 | any version | No decode-time gate. A parse failure is E237; `validate_for_intent` accepts version 1 only. |
| `ReleaseRunEnvelopeV1` | inside a receipt only | 3 | 3 | Rejected at decode with an `UnsupportedSchema` error that has no diagnostic code. |
| `ReleaseReceiptV1` | `release --receipt`, `release execute --receipt`; also the JSON stdout of both | 2 | 2 | Rejected at decode with an `UnsupportedSchema` error that has no diagnostic code. |

- The decision digest covers the sorted entries (package, target version, reasons) and not the schema version, so a version 1 and a version 2 decision with the same entries share a digest. The digest is verified on every read.
- A receipt is written only when every operation ended `published` or `alreadySatisfied`; a failed run leaves none.
- The release-PR documents (`ReleasePrSnapshotV2`, `ReleasePrDecisionV2`, `ReleasePrConfigV1`, `ReleasePrCommitPlanV1`) are separate types read and written by `release-pr decide`, `release-pr verify` and `release-pr commit-plan`, not by the release decision above. Each accepts exactly its own version. The config, snapshot and decision fail with E155; the commit plan fails with a plain message that has no code.

## Rerun with an older intent

A rerun never reuses an intent from another build. `release execute --intent` and `release artifact-manifest --intent` read the file first and fail with E215 when its version is not 5, before the run envelope is minted. The help says to run `release plan` again. The execution state that older builds persisted was removed; a state file from an older build is ignored, not read or migrated.

## Readers outside the model crate

- Shell and `jq` readers carry no version gate and depend on shape: the release workflow reads `.artifactSlots` from the intent, the generated build-matrix workflow reads `.operations[].id.package` and `.artifactSlots[]`, and `run-release.sh` reads the receipt's outcome paths.
- `release-pr` snapshots are built by `create-or-update-release-pr.sh` with a hard-coded `schemaVersion: 2`, while the action's `version` input can pin another binary.
- The standalone JSON stdout of `release` and `release execute` flattens the receipt and carries its schema version; the nothing-to-release report is a separate shape with version 1.

## Known gaps

- The snapshot and the artifact manifest have no decode-time version gate of their own.
- The intent decoder's check of the nested decision version cannot fail for a decoded decision, because the decision's decoder normalizes its version to 2 first.
- Two readers tightened without a version bump: the artifact attestation's `sourceCommit` now equals the slot's workflow commit rather than the release source, and decision, operation and slot versions parse with the owning package's ecosystem grammar.
- The receipt's version does not track its nested types: the envelope went from 1 to 3 and the operation role vocabulary grew while the receipt stayed at 2.
- No production code decodes a receipt or an envelope from bytes. Their decode gates and the receipt schema are exercised by tests only.
- A version 1 decision can carry an `unreleasedVersion` reason, which only version 2 defines, and nothing rejects it.
- `callisto schema --type release-receipt` is the only published release schema, and its `schemaVersion` is an unconstrained integer. `callisto schema --type snapshot` is the status report, not `ReleaseInputSnapshotV1`.
- The version 2 intent never existed as its own commit, and the digest transcript version is one constant shared by the decision, snapshot, intent and registry-binding digests.
- The generated consumer workflow passes the intent and manifest between jobs without a checksum or comparison step, which this repository's own release workflow has.

4	
5	## Two phases
6	
7	| Phase | Entry point | Touches disk |
8	| --- | --- | --- |
9	| Plan | `commands::plan_version` (`crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/version.rs`) returns a `VersionPlan` | No |
10	| Apply | `apply_version_plan` (`crates/callisto-graph/src/apply.rs`) | Yes; takes `&ApplyPermit` |
11	
12	- `VersionPlan` (`crates/callisto-graph/src/plan.rs`) is the whole change: bumps, dependency spec rewrites, platform manifest writes, owner `optionalDependencies` pins, changelog sections, consumed changesets, `pre.json` updates and diagnostics. It is in memory only (no `Serialize`).
13	- `plan_version` is shared: `version`, `status`, `compose-pr-body` and `release plan --package` all compute the same plan.
14	- A dry run never gets a permit, so it reports the plan and never calls apply.
15	- `snapshot` applies with `ApplyOptions::transient`: manifests are written, while changelogs, changeset deletion and git staging are skipped.
16	
17	## Idempotent apply
18	
19	A crash can stop apply after some files are written. Applying the same in-memory plan again is file-level idempotent; a fresh command does not retain that plan.
20	
21	- Each `PlannedBump` carries `from` and `to`. Before writing a manifest (or a platform manifest), apply reads its current version: `from` means write, `to` means already done, anything else is `UnexpectedManifestVersion`.
22	- A manifest already at `to` is still staged: the crashed run may have written it without `git add`.
23	- Apply refreshes affected lockfiles and stages generated version state before consuming changesets or exiting `pre.json`. It stages input deletions with `git rm --cached --ignore-unmatch` before removing the files from disk, so a failed index update leaves the inputs available for recovery. A fresh command does not retain the in-memory plan and can refuse already-stable staged outputs; E121 directs the user to inspect both diffs and finish consuming retained inputs only when the staged outputs are verified. Automatic replay is not guaranteed.
24	- `[workspace.package]` version writes (`VersionWriteTarget::CargoWorkspacePackage`) have no `from`/`to` precondition; they are written unconditionally.
25	- `ApplyOutcome::staged` lists every path apply staged.
26	
27	## Command boundary and known gaps
28	
29	`version --emit-decision` derives and validates the decision before writes, applies the plan, and writes the decision only after apply succeeds. The decision file is not wrapped in the stdout report envelope.
30	
31	Outside `mode: pre`, `check_partial_run` refuses with E121 when a canonical manifest's effective version differs from `HEAD` while a changeset remains in `HEAD` or in the working tree (including untracked files), or when a canonical manifest with an effective staged version change is present in the index. Staged metadata-only edits are allowed. During `mode: exit`, prerelease versions awaiting stable finalization remain eligible, but changed stable versions are not exempt from the retry guard. It does not restore a lost plan. Apply retains changesets and pre-state deletion inputs until lock refresh and staging of generated state succeed, then stages their removal before unlinking them from disk. A late `--emit-decision` write failure is actionable refusal, not automatic replay of an in-memory plan that no longer exists.
32	
33	Apply refreshes each existing lockfile for every ecosystem represented by an actual version, dependency, platform or optional-dependency write, including dual-manifest packages and workspace-root Cargo writes. Cargo lockfiles are refreshed and staged per Cargo workspace, in that workspace's directory. Dependency cascade, co-release floor and snapshot rewrites resolve names in each declaration's native manifest context; pnpm workspace protocols and aliases remain distinct inputs. ## Two phases

| Phase | Entry point | Touches disk |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Plan | `commands::plan_version` (`crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/version.rs`) returns a `VersionPlan` | No |
| Apply | `apply_version_plan` (`crates/callisto-graph/src/apply.rs`) | Yes; takes `&ApplyPermit` |

- `VersionPlan` (`crates/callisto-graph/src/plan.rs`) is the whole change: bumps, dependency spec rewrites, platform manifest writes, owner `optionalDependencies` pins, changelog sections, consumed changesets, `pre.json` updates and diagnostics. It is in memory only (no `Serialize`).
- `plan_version` is shared: `version`, `status`, `compose-pr-body` and `release plan --package` all compute the same plan.
- A dry run never gets a permit, so it reports the plan and never calls apply.
- `snapshot` applies with `ApplyOptions::transient`: manifests are written, while changelogs, changeset deletion and git staging are skipped.

## Idempotent apply

A crash can stop apply after some files are written. Applying the same in-memory plan again is file-level idempotent; a fresh command does not retain that plan.

- Each `PlannedBump` carries `from` and `to`. Before writing a manifest (or a platform manifest), apply reads its current version: `from` means write, `to` means already done, anything else is `UnexpectedManifestVersion`.
- A manifest already at `to` is still staged: the crashed run may have written it without `git add`.
- Apply refreshes affected lockfiles and stages generated version state before consuming changesets or exiting `pre.json`. It stages input deletions with `git rm --cached --ignore-unmatch` before removing the files from disk, so a failed index update leaves the inputs available for recovery. A fresh command does not retain the in-memory plan and can refuse already-stable staged outputs; E121 directs the user to inspect both diffs and finish consuming retained inputs only when the staged outputs are verified. Automatic replay is not guaranteed.
- `[workspace.package]` version writes (`VersionWriteTarget::CargoWorkspacePackage`) have no `from`/`to` precondition; they are written unconditionally.
- `ApplyOutcome::staged` lists every path apply staged.

## Command boundary and known gaps

`version --emit-decision` derives and validates the decision before writes, applies the plan, and writes the decision only after apply succeeds. The decision file is not wrapped in the stdout report envelope.

Outside `mode: pre`, `check_partial_run` refuses with E121 when a canonical manifest's effective version differs from `HEAD` while a changeset remains in `HEAD` or in the working tree (including untracked files), or when a canonical manifest with an effective staged version change is present in the index. Staged metadata-only edits are allowed. During `mode: exit`, prerelease versions awaiting stable finalization remain eligible, but changed stable versions are not exempt from the retry guard. It does not restore a lost plan. Apply retains changesets and pre-state deletion inputs until lock refresh and staging of generated state succeed, then stages their removal before unlinking them from disk. A late `--emit-decision` write failure is actionable refusal, not automatic replay of an in-memory plan that no longer exists.

Apply refreshes each existing lockfile for every ecosystem represented by an actual version, dependency, platform or optional-dependency write, including dual-manifest packages and workspace-root Cargo writes. Cargo lockfiles are refreshed and staged per Cargo workspace, in that workspace's directory. Dependency cascade, co-release floor and snapshot rewrites resolve names in each declaration's native manifest context; pnpm workspace protocols and aliases remain distinct inputs. 1	# Scoped polyglot release model
2	
3	Status: proposed v1 design, not current behavior. Owner scope: Rust/Cargo, npm/pnpm and Python/PyPI now; leave room for Go and .NET/NuGet without implementing their publishers. Current contracts remain in [the specs](../specs/INDEX.md). Work is sequenced in [the roadmap](../projects/ROAD-TO-V1.md) and [the plan](../projects/V1-SYSTEM-HARDENING.json).
4	
5	## Four concepts
6	
7	| Concept | Responsibility | Not equivalent to |
8	| --- | --- | --- |
9	| Release owner | Source/version authority and the outputs released together | A display name or registry destination |
10	| Distribution | Canonical ecosystem-qualified identity and native package name | A source directory or import/module name |
11	| Version authority | Literal or supported inherited/derived source, plus each distribution's native representation | A grammar guessed from a JSON string |
12	| Release effect | One required external effect, its destination, evidence and prerequisites | A package tag proving all publications finished |
13	
14	Keep existing types where they already express these responsibilities. A `PackageKey` locates a directory; it does not prove identity survives a directory move. Do not add opaque IDs or a public plugin protocol without a demonstrated need. The release owner is derived from existing types and sealed by the intent digest; no owner field or wire change is needed for the current scope.
15	
16	## Canonical references and migration
17	
18	- Configuration, generated config, machine reports and command-line arguments use only canonical `cargo/name`, `npm/@scope/name` or `pypi/name` references; bare and colon-form aliases are rejected. Changesets and `pre.json` keep native package names, resolved when read, because an entry names an owner package and the files stay readable by `@changesets/cli`. Native normalization belongs to the ecosystem; Python distribution names are not import names, and a `pypi/` reference uses the declared name.
19	- Short labels may remain in human output, but never become an alternate identity authority. Ecosystem-specific native names stay available for manifest rewrites and publisher arguments.
20	- A bare name in a changeset or `pre.json` resolves through established ownership; ambiguous input fails with an actionable diagnostic. Persisted release documents are already canonical-only.
21	- Adding or removing a same-named sibling, adding a canonical manifest or changing the primary manifest must not transfer another owner's history or regress the last release. A genuine rename/move needs a declared migration boundary, not guessing from current path existence.
22	- Keep [ADR 11](../adr/0011-directory-keyed-package-identity.md) in force, including its default tag `{display id}@{version}`, until [the proposed replacement](../adr/0012-canonical-distribution-release-ownership.md) is implemented and accepted. Do not rename existing tags to canonicalize selectors; a native rename is declared with `previous-tag-templates`.
23	
24	## Native versions and dependencies
25	
26	A release owner can have several distribution outputs. Shared versioning is deliberate; co-location or a build dependency alone does not require version coupling. Co-located Cargo/Maturin is after v1; today it fails with E007, and separate-directory Cargo and Python packages are supported. The design for it: Cargo is the version authority and the Python distribution uses `dynamic = ["version"]`. Maturin does not map versions; it parses the Cargo version as PEP 440, so Callisto computes the expected Python version with the `pep440_rs` crate and verifies the built metadata. Several SemVer prereleases are not faithful in PEP 440 (`pre`, `c` and `rc` collapse to `rc`; `dev` and `post` change the sort order; `+build` is a local version PyPI rejects), so accept only stable and `-alpha.N`, `-beta.N`, `-rc.N` and refuse the rest, and snapshots, before any write. Refuse a static Python version beside Cargo, which maturin does not check. Do not introduce a universal reversible version converter or arbitrary SCM-derived backends.
27	
28	Reuse the native dependency graph and derived release-operation DAG. Preserve each edge's manifest, declared key/alias, resolved distribution, constraint and dependency kind. A native Cargo edge must not become a dependency on every distribution produced by the same source package.
29	
30	- Native registry dependency: update that ecosystem's reference and derive only relevant publication prerequisites. Range coverage, version cascade and publication order are distinct decisions.
31	- Embedded/build input: the consuming artifact needs those bytes or sources. It does not necessarily need that input published to Cargo, npm or PyPI. Builders and CI retain build ordering; add explicit cross-project input relationships only for a supported concrete case.
32	- Version coupling: retain fixed/linked policies separately from dependency edges; do not infer a major bump of every wrapper from an internal-language change.
33	- Runtime services and arbitrary cross-language discovery are outside the release graph's scope.
34	
35	For pnpm, retain the difference between `workspace:*`, explicit workspace ranges, aliases, relative paths and catalogs. Let pnpm perform pack-time transformations. For Python, preserve extras, markers and native specifiers; document direct-URL and dynamic-backend support rather than treating them as ordinary ranges. Cargo inherited versions/dependencies require their authoritative root paths in both live and historical reads.
36	
37	## Effects and completion
38	
39	For current registry ecosystems, the proposed default is required registry publications confirmed before a shared tag and public GitHub announcement. A draft and uploads may be preparatory effects; public publication waits for all required outputs of that release owner. Exact draft timing must be specified with the implementation. This is Callisto's policy, not a universal ecosystem order.
40	
41	Within Callisto's release-operation graph, one physical tag, forge release or upload has one owner even when several distributions share it. Native package-manager lifecycle hooks retain package-owner-defined behavior and environment. Callisto does not inspect, rewrite, suppress or reject those hooks; any effects they initiate are outside Callisto's graph and remain the package owner's responsibility. For example, NAPI `prepublishOnly` may publish platform packages or GitHub assets while Callisto also performs configured release effects.
42	
43	A retry retains the authorized roster and observes every remaining effect, even when its tag or some registry files already exist. Keep execution state in memory; the immutable intent, original artifact manifest and providers supply recovery evidence. No journal, automatic version bump, destructive rollback or changed replacement bytes under an already-published version.
44	
45	PyPI completion is the declared file set for the release, not the first matching wheel or sdist. Required platform packages must exist before their npm owner publishes. Missing, conflicting, yanked and unobservable results must not be collapsed into complete success. Use hashes where needed to distinguish intended files from conflicting bytes; do not make an unapproved universal registry-checksum requirement a v1 gate.
46	
47	Registry identity is separate from read/upload routes and native authentication configuration. Specify public PyPI first; decide authenticated private indexes and HTML-only indexes explicitly. Mutable npm dist-tags are channel labels, not distribution versions; channel verification/promotion policy is an owner decision, not implicit rollback.
48	
49	## Future compatibility examples
50	
51	- Go: a source tag is a publication effect; a v2+ module generally has a new major-qualified module path, and subdirectory modules need their native tag prefix. Do not require every ecosystem to publish before its source tag or carry its version in a manifest.
52	- NuGet: package-version normalization differs from SemVer; package version is not assembly/file version. A single package can contain runtime-identifier and target-framework assets. Do not assume every native target is a Rust triple or every platform is a separate distribution.
53	- Cross-language wrappers: native libraries, subprocess tools and generated bindings are concrete inputs to a native distribution, not foreign package-manager dependency entries. Building Rust into a Python wheel does not by itself require a crates.io publication.
54	
55	These are model checks only. Go/NuGet discovery, rewriting, packing, authentication and publication remain deferred.
56	
57	## Prior art and research limits
58	
59	| Tool | Established approach | Boundary relevant to Callisto |
60	| --- | --- | --- |
61	| Changesets | npm/pnpm graph-based publication, then tags for successful publications | Native JS release semantics, not a cross-registry transaction. [Publisher](https://github.com/changesets/changesets/blob/main/packages/cli/src/commands/publish/index.ts) |
62	| Knope | Several versioned files can form one release package | Cargo+Python ownership stays simple; Python dependency rewriting is not supported by its documented format handler. [Ownership](https://knope.tech/tutorials/releasing-multiple-packages/), [formats](https://knope.tech/reference/config-file/packages/) |
63	| Nx Release | Project identities, release groups and ecosystem VersionActions/publishers | Reuse the separation, not the general build framework. Its Rust recipe still documents a legacy-versioning restriction; current plugin compatibility needs a runtime check. [Configuration](https://nx.dev/docs/reference/nx-json), [Rust recipe](https://nx.dev/docs/kb/publish-rust-crates) |
64	| release-please | Polyglot strategies, native workspace plugins and separate registry publishing | Its example publishes npm after tags/releases already exist; that is not Callisto's required completion policy. [Manifest model](https://github.com/googleapis/release-please/blob/main/docs/manifest-releaser.md) |
65	
66	Sources checked on 2026-09-26: [Maturin version authority](https://www.maturin.rs/metadata), [pnpm workspace transformations](https://pnpm.io/workspaces), [catalogs](https://pnpm.io/catalogs), [Python name normalization](https://packaging.python.org/en/latest/specifications/name-normalization/), [PEP 440](https://packaging.python.org/en/latest/specifications/version-specifiers/), [PyPI one-file uploads](https://docs.pypi.org/api/upload/), [per-file index evidence](https://packaging.python.org/en/latest/specifications/simple-repository-api/), [NAPI publication hooks](https://napi.rs/docs/cli/pre-publish), [Go module versions](https://go.dev/doc/modules/version-numbers), [NuGet normalization](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/nuget/concepts/package-versioning), [NuGet native assets](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/nuget/create-packages/native-files-in-net-packages).
67	
68	Competitor release workflows were inspected, not executed. Fresh co-located static and dynamic Cargo/Maturin discovery fixtures both reproduced E007, and the maturin 1.15.0 metadata hook agreed with `pep440_rs` on every version tried. Native pack/install tests and partial-upload fault injection remain planned; see [the findings register](../projects/V1-FINDINGS.md).
69	
70	## Non-goals
71	
72	No universal package manager, build scheduler, five public graph types, arbitrary interoperability inference, external service graph, cross-registry atomic transaction, public adapter framework or persisted execution-state mechanism. Expand the model only when a supported fixture demonstrates a missing responsibility.
73

Refuse a static Python version beside Cargo, which maturin does not check. Do not introduce a universal reversible version converter or arbitrary SCM-derived backends.

Reuse the native dependency graph and derived release-operation DAG. Preserve each edge's manifest, declared key/alias, resolved distribution, constraint and dependency kind. A native Cargo edge must not become a dependency on every distribution produced by the same source package.

- Native registry dependency: update that ecosystem's reference and derive only relevant publication prerequisites. Range coverage, version cascade and publication order are distinct decisions.
- Embedded/build input: the consuming artifact needs those bytes or sources. It does not necessarily need that input published to Cargo, npm or PyPI. Builders and CI retain build ordering; add explicit cross-project input relationships only for a supported concrete case.
- Version coupling: retain fixed/linked policies separately from dependency edges; do not infer a major bump of every wrapper from an internal-language change.
- Runtime services and arbitrary cross-language discovery are outside the release graph's scope.

For pnpm, retain the difference between `workspace:*`, explicit workspace ranges, aliases, relative paths and catalogs. Let pnpm perform pack-time transformations. For Python, preserve extras, markers and native specifiers; document direct-URL and dynamic-backend support rather than treating them as ordinary ranges. Cargo inherited versions/dependencies require their authoritative root paths in both live and historical reads.

## Effects and completion

For current registry ecosystems, the proposed default is required registry publications confirmed before a shared tag and public GitHub announcement. A draft and uploads may be preparatory effects; public publication waits for all required outputs of that release owner. Exact draft timing must be specified with the implementation. This is Callisto's policy, not a universal ecosystem order.

Within Callisto's release-operation graph, one physical tag, forge release or upload has one owner even when several distributions share it. Native package-manager lifecycle hooks retain package-owner-defined behavior and environment. Callisto does not inspect, rewrite, suppress or reject those hooks; any effects they initiate are outside Callisto's graph and remain the package owner's responsibility. For example, NAPI `prepublishOnly` may publish platform packages or GitHub assets while Callisto also performs configured release effects.

A retry retains the authorized roster and observes every remaining effect, even when its tag or some registry files already exist. Keep execution state in memory; the immutable intent, original artifact manifest and providers supply recovery evidence. No journal, automatic version bump, destructive rollback or changed replacement bytes under an already-published version.

PyPI completion is the declared file set for the release, not the first matching wheel or sdist. Required platform packages must exist before their npm owner publishes. Missing, conflicting, yanked and unobservable results must not be collapsed into complete success. Use hashes where needed to distinguish intended files from conflicting bytes; do not make an unapproved universal registry-checksum requirement a v1 gate.

Registry identity is separate from read/upload routes and native authentication configuration. Specify public PyPI first; decide authenticated private indexes and HTML-only indexes explicitly. Mutable npm dist-tags are channel labels, not distribution versions; channel verification/promotion policy is an owner decision, not implicit rollback.

## Future compatibility examples

- Go: a source tag is a publication effect; a v2+ module generally has a new major-qualified module path, and subdirectory modules need their native tag prefix. Do not require every ecosystem to publish before its source tag or carry its version in a manifest.
- NuGet: package-version normalization differs from SemVer; package version is not assembly/file version. A single package can contain runtime-identifier and target-framework assets. Do not assume every native target is a Rust triple or every platform is a separate distribution.
- Cross-language wrappers: native libraries, subprocess tools and generated bindings are concrete inputs to a native distribution, not foreign package-manager dependency entries. Building Rust into a Python wheel does not by itself require a crates.io publication.

These are model checks only. Go/NuGet discovery, rewriting, packing, authentication and publication remain deferred.

## Prior art and research limits

| Tool | Established approach | Boundary relevant to Callisto |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Changesets | npm/pnpm graph-based publication, then tags for successful publications | Native JS release semantics, not a cross-registry transaction. [Publisher](https://github.com/changesets/changesets/blob/main/packages/cli/src/commands/publish/index.ts) |
| Knope | Several versioned files can form one release package | Cargo+Python ownership stays simple; Python dependency rewriting is not supported by its documented format handler. [Ownership](https://knope.tech/tutorials/releasing-multiple-packages/), [formats](https://knope.tech/reference/config-file/packages/) |
| Nx Release | Project identities, release groups and ecosystem VersionActions/publishers | Reuse the separation, not the general build framework. Its Rust recipe still documents a legacy-versioning restriction; current plugin compatibility needs a runtime check. [Configuration](https://nx.dev/docs/reference/nx-json), [Rust recipe](https://nx.dev/docs/kb/publish-rust-crates) |
| release-please | Polyglot strategies, native workspace plugins and separate registry publishing | Its example publishes npm after tags/releases already exist; that is not Callisto's required completion policy. [Manifest model](https://github.com/googleapis/release-please/blob/main/docs/manifest-releaser.md) |

Sources checked on 2026-09-26: [Maturin version authority](https://www.maturin.rs/metadata), [pnpm workspace transformations](https://pnpm.io/workspaces), [catalogs](https://pnpm.io/catalogs), [Python name normalization](https://packaging.python.org/en/latest/specifications/name-normalization/), [PEP 440](https://packaging.python.org/en/latest/specifications/version-specifiers/), [PyPI one-file uploads](https://docs.pypi.org/api/upload/), [per-file index evidence](https://packaging.python.org/en/latest/specifications/simple-repository-api/), [NAPI publication hooks](https://napi.rs/docs/cli/pre-publish), [Go module versions](https://go.dev/doc/modules/version-numbers), [NuGet normalization](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/nuget/concepts/package-versioning), [NuGet native assets](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/nuget/create-packages/native-files-in-net-packages).

Competitor release workflows were inspected, not executed. Fresh co-located static and dynamic Cargo/Maturin discovery fixtures both reproduced E007, and the maturin 1.15.0 metadata hook agreed with `pep440_rs` on every version tried. Native pack/install tests and partial-upload fault injection remain planned; see [the findings register](../projects/V1-FINDINGS.md).

## Non-goals

No universal package manager, build scheduler, five public graph types, arbitrary interoperability inference, external service graph, cross-registry atomic transaction, public adapter framework or persisted execution-state mechanism. Expand the model only when a supported fixture demonstrates a missing responsibility.

Callisto Architecture

2 3

Crate map, data flow, and the invariants every change must preserve.

4 5 --- 6 7 ## Invariants 8 9 1. **Safe Rust only.** `unsafe_code = "forbid"` workspace-wide. 10 2. **License boundary.** `callisto-model` is MIT and must never depend on an FSL-1.1-MIT crate. Every other crate is FSL-1.1-MIT. Check with `grep -H "^license" crates/*/Cargo.toml`. 11 3. **Format-preserving manifest edits.** `Cargo.toml` goes through `toml_edit`'s CST; `package.json` is fingerprinted for indent style and line endings before a `serde_json` (`preserve_order`) round trip. No regex or line-based edits to manifests. 12 4. **One file-write primitive, capability-gated.** `callisto_model::atomic::atomic_write` (`NamedTempFile` in the target's own directory, `fsync`, `persist` via `fs::rename`, then `fsync` the parent directory, and its parent when the call created it; a failed sync is returned unless the filesystem cannot sync a directory) is the only way file content is written; deletions and directory creation use `std::fs`. It takes `&ApplyPermit`, a token with a private field that only `ApplyPermit::granted_unless_dry_run(dry_run)` can construct, returning `None` on a dry run. A write path that forgets to check `--dry-run` has no permit to pass and fails to compile. 13 5. **System Git only.** All VCS reads and writes shell out to the user's `git` binary (`callisto_model::vcs`), so Callisto sees exactly the repository, config, and identity Git itself does. No embedded Git implementation. 14 6. **Versioning.** The four published crates version in lockstep (one fixed group). Only `callisto-cli`, its command-line interface and its JSON reports are a compatibility surface; `callisto-model`, `callisto-manifests` and `callisto-graph` are internal and may change in any release. 15 7. **User-facing errors are diagnosable.** Every error surfaced to a user derives `miette::Diagnostic` with a stable code and, where the fix isn't obvious from the message, `help` text. A wrapper around another crate's error (for example `GraphError::Config`) is `#[diagnostic(transparent)]` and declares no code of its own, so the inner code reaches the user. Full list: [`docs/errors.md`](docs/errors.md). 16 17 Design decisions, with the options they rejected and why: [`docs/adr/README.md`](docs/adr/README.md). 18 19 ## Crate map 20 21 ``` 22 Layer 1 (leaf) callisto-model 23 Layer 2 (I/O) callisto-manifests 24 Layer 3 (engine) callisto-graph 25 Layer 4 (surface) callisto-cli 26 Dev-only callisto-fixtures 27 ``` 28 29 | Crate | License | Depends on | Purpose | 30 | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | 31 | [`callisto-model`](crates/callisto-model) | MIT | none (external: `michi-graph`) | Domain primitives (`PackageId`, `Version`, `Severity`, `Changeset`, `PreState`), `atomic_write`, `ApplyPermit`, the `CommandRunner`/`DependencyResolver` trait seams; `format`: `.changeset/*.md` and `pre.json` parser/writer; `vcs`: `GitAccess`, every Git operation as a subprocess through `CommandRunner` | 32 | [`callisto-manifests`](crates/callisto-manifests) | FSL-1.1-MIT | model | `Manifest` trait; format-preserving Cargo/npm/PyPI manifest editors | 33 | [`callisto-graph`](crates/callisto-graph) | FSL-1.1-MIT | model, manifests | Dependency graph, cascade engine, version planning, release execution; `conventional`: Conventional Commit parsing and bump inference; `changelog`: Markdown changelog rendering | 34 | [`callisto-cli`](crates/callisto-cli) | FSL-1.1-MIT | model, manifests, graph | `clap` CLI surface, `miette` diagnostic rendering | 35 | [`callisto-fixtures`](crates/callisto-fixtures) | FSL-1.1-MIT | model (dev-only) | Multi-ecosystem test corpus and in-memory test doubles | 36 37 Dependencies only point down the layers (`cli` → `graph` → `manifests` → `model`). Nothing in Layer 1–3 depends on `callisto-cli`. 38 39 ## Data flow 40 41 ``` 42 Workspace::load 43 config::load -> config::resolve callisto.toml -> ResolvedConfig 44 ManifestWalkResolver::build discover (ProjectLocator), read manifests (Manifest), 45 assign ids, attach platform packages, apply per-package config 46 GroupTable::resolve bind [[fixed-group]] / [[linked-group]] members 47 plan_version -> VersionPlan (in memory) 48 aggregate changesets + opt-in commit inference -> severity per package 49 run_cascade dependents (runtime, build, optional, peer; never dev), groups, pre mode 50 -> target version per package, with its reasons 51 version --emit-decision derives and validates the decision in memory, before apply 52 apply_version_plan (needs ApplyPermit) CST edits -> atomic_write, changelogs 53 consume changesets -> native lock refresh -> git staging 54 version --emit-decision writes the decision file after successful apply 55 release decision -> intent -> envelope -> execute_release -> receipt 56 per operation observe provider -> adopt, or perform and confirm 57 ``` 58 59 Package ordering, cycle reports and release-operation readiness all run on `michi-graph` (validation reports every problem at once; edge kinds are chosen per validation). Git access goes through `GitAccess` (`callisto_model::vcs`). 60 61 Depth: 62 63 - [`docs/architecture/identity.md`](docs/architecture/identity.md): package ids, bare-name matching, config rule specificity, workspace loading, platform packages. 64 - [`docs/architecture/versioning.md`](docs/architecture/versioning.md): plan and apply, file-level idempotence and interrupted-command limits. 65 - [`docs/architecture/release.md`](docs/architecture/release.md): release terms, the two routes, run envelope, observation and proof tokens, the transition table, verification tiers. 66 - [`docs/architecture/wire-compat.md`](docs/architecture/wire-compat.md): the version each release document writes and reads, what a reader does with another, and the known gaps. 67 68 ## Extension seams 69 70 Four traits decouple the engine from platform I/O (`callisto-model::exec`, `callisto-model::discovery`, `callisto-manifests`, `callisto-graph::locate`): 71 72 - `ProjectLocator` — enumerates workspace project roots. 73 - `CommandRunner` — runs a subprocess. `run_with_timeout`'s default implementation ignores the timeout; the CLI's runner enforces it, so a hung publish command cannot block forever. 74 - `Manifest` — per-ecosystem read/write. Mutations only touch the in-memory CST; nothing reaches disk until `persist(&ApplyPermit)`, so one open manifest can take several mutations before one write. 75 - `DependencyResolver` — supplies graph nodes and edges; `ManifestWalkResolver` is the only current implementation. 76 77 ## Current boundaries and planned changes 78 79 `PackageId` is a flexible selector/display form; `PackageKey` is a directory locator; `ReleasePackageId` is a canonical ecosystem-qualified distribution identity. A directory can own several canonical manifests, but the current package model requires one version grammar. Registry version observations do not establish a complete Python file set or identical package bytes. 80 81 Known contract failures and verification gaps are tracked in [`docs/projects/V1-FINDINGS.md`](docs/projects/V1-FINDINGS.md). The proposed canonical-identity and polyglot model is in [`docs/architecture/polyglot-v1.md`](docs/architecture/polyglot-v1.md); it is not an implemented extension seam. The existing dependency graph and release-operation DAG remain the basis of the plan. 82 83 ## Not covered here 84 85 - Release lifecycle, CI plan/build/execute, recovery: [`docs/releasing.md`](docs/releasing.md). 86 - Registry authentication: [`docs/publishing.md`](docs/publishing.md). 87 - `callisto.toml` keys: [`docs/config.md`](docs/config.md). 88 - Diagnostic codes: [`docs/errors.md`](docs/errors.md). 89 - Behavior, including `callisto matrix`: [`docs/specs/`](docs/specs/INDEX.md). 90

1	# Architecture decision records
2	
3	- [1. Changesets-compatible change records](0001-changesets-compatible-change-records.md) — `.changeset/*.md` in `@changesets/cli`'s format, commit inference opt-in; guardrail: do not make Conventional Commits the primary input or change the file format without a new ADR.
4	- [2. The committed version decision is the release authority](0002-committed-decision-is-release-authority.md) — CI verifies the merged commit against the decision `callisto version --emit-decision` committed; guardrail: do not re-derive cascade or group policy after merge without a new ADR.
5	- [3. Reruns observe and adopt landed effects; no persisted execution state](0003-reruns-adopt-landed-effects.md) — every run observes providers and adopts what landed, state stays in memory; guardrail: do not add a persisted execution state file or recovery commands without a new ADR.
6	- [4. Ecosystem tools publish and own authentication](0004-ecosystem-tools-publish-and-own-auth.md) — `cargo`, the npm-family tools, `twine` and `gh` publish with their own credentials; guardrail: do not add native registry clients or a credential pre-flight without a new ADR.
7	- [5. System git only](0005-system-git-only.md) — every Git command in the `callisto` binary runs the system `git`; guardrail: do not add gix or a second Git backend without a new ADR.
8	- [6. moon integrates through a proto plugin, not a WASM extension](0006-moon-through-proto-plugin-not-wasm-extension.md) — moon users install the native CLI with a proto TOML plugin; guardrail: do not add a moon WASM extension or WASM build without a new ADR.
9	- [7. Platform packages are owned through optionalDependencies and release with their owner](0007-platform-packages-owned-through-optional-dependencies.md) — an `os`+`cpu` package with one owner releases with that owner; guardrail: do not require fixed-group entries or explicit config for platform packages without a new ADR.
10	- [8. Format-preserving manifest writes gated by ApplyPermit](0008-format-preserving-writes-gated-by-apply-permit.md) — `toml_edit` and fingerprinted JSON through `atomic_write(&ApplyPermit)`; guardrail: do not use typed serde round-trips for TOML, unfingerprinted `package.json` rewrites, regex edits or unpermitted writes without a new ADR.
11	- [9. A tag's identity is its commit and being annotated](0009-tag-identity-is-commit-and-annotation.md) — an existing annotated tag on the planned commit is adopted whatever its message; guardrail: do not compare annotation text or accept lightweight tags without a new ADR.
12	- [10. The workspace resolves natively after `version` or `snapshot`](0010-native-resolution-after-version.md) — a co-released dependent's spec is always raised to the new version and lockfiles refresh by default; guardrail: do not go back to rewriting only out-of-range specs or make lockfile refresh opt-in without a new ADR.
13	- [11. Directory-keyed packages and promotion-aware history](0011-directory-keyed-package-identity.md) — the directory key survives display promotion; new default tags use the promoted display id and historical bare records use an ownership fallback; guardrail: do not derive paths or persisted keys from the display id without a new ADR.
14	- [12. Canonical distribution references and explicit release ownership](0012-canonical-distribution-release-ownership.md) — proposed v1 correction; not accepted or implemented. Separates native distribution identities, version authority and shared effects while preserving deliberate historical migration.
15	
16	## Rules
17	
18	- An ADR records an architecturally significant decision that had a credible alternative.
19	- `Proposed` until the PR that implements it merges, then `Accepted`.
20	- A changed decision gets a new ADR with `Status: Supersedes N`. The old file moves to `docs/adr/superseded/` with `Status: Superseded by M`. Agents do not load that folder.
21	- Every reason cites a source (commit, PR, historical doc). If none exists, write "Reason not recorded".
22	- Behaviour belongs in `docs/specs/`; coding rules belong in `AGENTS.md`.
